title: Sprint Retro: Provision-to-Ready Automation (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
author: Talia Benson
content:
## Summary
This sprint delivered an automated “provision-to-ready” workflow for Dedicated capacity bring-up, including a persisted provisioning state machine, standardized eventing/metrics, initial config validation gates (with audited break-glass), readiness smoke tests + perf-canary, and routing “Ready-only” consumption.

Across the pilot pools we reduced median time-to-ready and removed the largest operator handoffs (manual “is it safe to route?” checks). We also surfaced several reliability gaps around helm values hygiene, region-specific imaging latency, and schema edge cases.

## Sprint goals (as committed)
1) Reduce time-to-ready for new Dedicated pools and expansions by automating the end-to-end lifecycle.
2) Make the bring-up predictable enough to support shorter Sales/CS ETAs.
3) Add readiness gates so routing only advertises capacity that is actually validated.
4) Provide stage-level observability (metrics + dashboard) and an operator-first runbook/CLI.

## What shipped (by deliverable)
### 1) Provisioning orchestration + state machine
- Implemented a persisted state machine for pool provisioning runs:
  - Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready / Failed
- Added audit trail for transitions and operator actions (pause/resume, break-glass).
- Added safe retry/backoff policy for imaging + bootstrap stages.

Operational impact:
- Reduced “where is this stuck?” ambiguity; operators now have a single canonical run status instead of chasing Terraform logs + cluster events.

### 2) IaC orchestration wrapper (idempotency + standardized outputs)
- Introduced a Terraform orchestration wrapper that:
  - consumes a consistent set of variables,
  - enforces idempotent apply for pool creation/expansion,
  - emits standardized outputs consumed by later stages (cluster endpoint, node groups, IAM role ARNs, pool identifiers).

### 3) Golden image + pinned runtime bootstrap hooks
- Hooked image build/promotion into the provisioning flow (pipeline can reference an approved image version).
- Pinned helm chart/runtime versions for bootstrap to reduce “worked last week” drift.

Note: Image hardening work is partially done; see “What didn’t ship”.

### 4) Config schema validation + policy gates
- Defined a pool config schema with validation + lint rules covering:
  - required fields (region, sku, node count bounds, network references)
  - known footguns (CIDR overlaps, invalid DNS/TLS toggles, inconsistent runtime flags)
  - “routing readiness” fields (canary thresholds, readiness suite config)
- Added a break-glass override mechanism with admin-only permissions and audit logging.

### 5) Readiness gates + perf-canary integration
- Added automated readiness checks before setting Ready:
  - GPU health checks (including ECC error detection)
  - networking/DNS/TLS checks
  - runtime smoke test
  - perf-canary “readiness suite” (minimal benchmark with pass/fail + summary)
- Fixed a race condition where Ready could be set before perf-canary completion (see incidents).

### 6) Observability + reporting
- Emitted structured provisioning events (stage start/finish/failure) with correlation IDs.
- Implemented time-to-ready metrics (overall + per-stage histograms) with cardinality safeguards.
- Built initial dashboard + alerts for stuck stages / high failure rate.
- Added Slack progress bot updates to #eng-infra (with links to runbook, logs, and dashboard panels).

### 7) Routing integration: “Ready means Ready”
- Updated routing to advertise Dedicated pools only when control plane marks them Ready.
- Added safety fallback and metrics to detect “capacity unexpectedly missing from routing due to readiness gating.”

## What didn’t ship / de-scoped
1) Full golden image hardening + provenance story (beyond initial hooks)
- We did not complete end-to-end artifact signing verification across all regions.
- We did not complete a compatibility matrix covering all supported GPU SKUs + runtime versions.
- Security review checklist exists in PRs, but we did not run a formal sign-off for every image variant.

2) Fully polished operator UX
- CLI works for core workflows (trigger run, re-run stage, dry-run), but:
  - error output is still too “internal” in some failure modes,
  - flags/argument discovery needs improvement,
  - “what changed from last run?” is missing.

3) Drift detection rollout
- Drift detection job exists and surfaces fields, but we did not operationalize response playbooks (what to do on drift) or enforce drift SLOs.

4) Customer self-serve UI
- As planned, no UI was built. Operators still trigger runs via CLI/API.

## Metrics & outcomes
### Time-to-ready (pilot pools)
Baseline was pulled from the prior 10 Dedicated bring-ups and compared to pilot runs.

**Overall (end-to-end):**
- Baseline p50: ~17.8 hours
- Baseline p95: ~46.5 hours
- Pilot p50: ~7.1 hours
- Pilot p95: ~19.6 hours

**Stage breakdown (median; baseline → pilot):**
- Provisioning (IaC): 2.4h → 1.6h
- Imaging: 6.2h → 2.8h (still volatile by region)
- Bootstrapping: 4.1h → 1.3h
- Validating (smoke + checks): 1.0h → 0.6h
- Perf-canary: N/A (manual/spot checks) → 0.4h

**Primary driver of improvement:** removing manual handoffs and standardizing bootstrap + validation; the remaining driver of variance is imaging timeouts and regional artifact availability.

### Reliability indicators
- First-pass success rate (pilot): 78% (target: 85%+)
  - Most failures were “actionable misconfig” (helm values) or “external/infra” (quota/IAM, image mirror latency).
- Mean retries per run: 1.3
- Top error categories (pilot):
  1) Helm values misconfiguration / chart incompatibility
  2) Imaging timeouts (region + SKU dependent)
  3) Terraform apply failures (quotas/IAM)
  4) GPU health failures (ECC)

## Incidents / notable pilot hiccups
### Incident A: Runs stuck in Bootstrapping due to misconfigured helm values
- Impact: multiple runs exceeded stage budget; blocked Ready marking; operators attempted manual fixes and caused partial drift.
- Root cause: a helm values template had an invalid default in one environment; bootstrap stage kept retrying but error classification did not surface the exact field quickly.
- Mitigation:
  - manual correction + re-run bootstrap stage
  - immediate doc update in provisioning runbook
- Follow-ups:
  - expand config validation to lint helm values for known required keys
  - improve bootstrap error messages with “action + runbook link” formatting

### Incident B: Ready set before perf-canary completion (race condition)
- Impact: brief window where routing could have advertised capacity that had not passed perf-canary; caught during pilot monitoring before customer traffic.
- Root cause: readiness transition did not transactionally depend on perf-canary result write.
- Fix: enforce ordering + transactional check; added integration tests for state transitions.

### Incident C: Imaging step slow/timeouts in one region (artifact mirror)
- Impact: imaging stage p95 remained high; operators reran imaging multiple times.
- Root cause: image artifact mirror saturation and occasional 5xx from region-local storage.
- Mitigation:
  - fallback to alternate mirror / prewarm where available
  - documented region-specific workaround
- Follow-ups:
  - implement detection for mirror degradation and automatic mirror fallback
  - prewarm images for planned expansions

### Incident D: Terraform apply failures (IAM/quotas) during staging pilot
- Impact: failed runs early in Provisioning stage; contributed to low first-pass rate.
- Root cause: missing IAM permission in staging role; quota checks were late.
- Mitigation:
  - fixed IAM policy and backfilled validation
- Follow-ups:
  - add preflight quota/IAM checks before terraform apply
  - clearer operator-facing error category: “blocking: quota/iam”

## What went well
- Cross-team alignment on Ready semantics was achieved early enough to implement routing gating safely.
- Correlation IDs + structured events materially improved debugging speed (SRE could answer “where did the time go?” quickly).
- Break-glass mechanism struck a good balance: it unblocked a legitimate edge-case config while preserving auditability.
- Stage re-run + pause/resume was heavily used by operators during pilot; prevented “start over from scratch.”

## What didn’t go well
- We underestimated the frequency of helm-values footguns and how much time they consume during bootstrap.
- Imaging remains the dominant source of variance; our stage budget assumed better regional consistency.
- Alerting noise: early “stuck stage” alerts fired during intentional pauses and during known retries.
- Slack bot update quality: duplicates and missing “next action” guidance caused confusion in #eng-infra.

## Decisions made during/after sprint
1) Routing must only consume Ready capacity; Validating is never routable.
2) Break-glass remains, but requires:
   - explicit reason string
   - auto-created ticket for review
   - time-bound allowlist where applicable
3) Alerting policy:
   - paging only for failures that block customer ETAs or indicate systemic outage
   - non-paging failures create tickets with run links and error category

## Appendix
### Pilot pools / scope
- Internal: 2 staging pools (multi-region)
- Customer: 1 expansion (observed during a coordinated window; capacity held out of routing until Ready)

### Artifacts shipped (high level)
- Provisioning state machine + persistence
- Control plane provisioning API endpoints
- Operator CLI
- Structured eventing + time-to-ready metrics
- Readiness gates + perf-canary readiness suite
- Routing “Ready-only” integration
- Dashboard + initial alerts

### Open questions
1) Should we prewarm images for “expected expansions” (sales forecast) by default, or only for high-tier customers?
2) Do we need separate Ready flavors (ReadyForRouting vs ReadyForCustomerValidation) for Private/VPC deployments, or keep a single global definition?
3) How strict should perf-canary thresholds be across heterogeneous SKUs (absolute vs normalized)?
